titulo: Unreal Past, Modal Perfect and Third Conditional
descripcion: Regret in English draws on three structures that learners usually meet in separate units: the unreal past after wish, the modal perfect (could/should/might have), and the third conditional. In real speech they blend into a single train of thought — I wish I'd known; we could have avoided it; if we'd checked, none of this would have happened — and the blending is the actual skill.

filas: if + past perfect, would have + participle

ejemplos.texto: I wish I'd known sooner — we could have avoided the whole mess.
If we'd checked the settings, this wouldn't have happened.
We should have asked; nobody thought to.

notas: These three often appear in sequence within the same paragraph: wish sets the regret, modal perfect names the missed action, the third conditional spells out the alternative.
Would have never appears in the if-clause of a third conditional, even though it's tempting after wish + would.
Could have and might have differ in confidence: could have is a genuine possibility, might have is more tentative.

es.en: Spanish expresses the same with si + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo and the conditional perfect, regret with ojalá + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo, and it also has the modal perfect (debería haberlo dicho, podría haberlo evitado). The logic is therefore parallel; the typical problem is the order of the pieces, since Spanish puts the modal in the conditional and English uses should have / could have + participle.
es.es: El español expresa lo mismo con «si» + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo y condicional compuesto, con «ojalá» + pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo para el arrepentimiento, y también dispone del modal perfecto («debería haberlo dicho», «podría haberlo evitado»). La lógica es paralela; el problema típico es el orden de los elementos, porque el español pone el modal en condicional y el inglés usa «should have / could have» + participio.

de.en: German has all three pieces with close equivalents: ich wünschte, ich hätte… (I wish I had…), hätte… sollen / können (should / could have) and the Konjunktiv II Plusquamperfekt in conditionals. The typical errors come from colloquial German würde: I wish I would have… and if I would have known….
de.de: Im Deutschen gibt es für alle drei Elemente nahe Entsprechungen: «ich wünschte, ich hätte…» («I wish I had…»), «hätte… sollen/können» («should/could have») und den Konjunktiv II Plusquamperfekt in Konditionalsätzen. Typische Fehler kommen aus umgangssprachlichem «würde»: «I wish I would have…» und «if I would have known…».

it.en: Italian has the modal perfect as a separate piece (avrei dovuto dirtelo, avrei potuto evitarlo), so the logic transfers well. Translated literally, however, avrei dovuto becomes I would have had to tell you, where English says I should have told you.
it.it: L'italiano ha un modal perfect separato («avrei dovuto dirtelo», «avrei potuto evitarlo»), quindi la logica si trasferisce bene. Tradotto letteralmente, però, «avrei dovuto» diventa «I would have had to tell you», dove l'inglese dice «I should have told you».

fr.en: French has the modal perfect (j'aurais dû le dire, j'aurais pu l'éviter) and si seulement j'avais su for regret, so the logic is parallel. Literal translation, however, turns j'aurais dû into I would have had to, where English uses should have.
fr.fr: Le français possède le modal perfect («j'aurais dû le dire», «j'aurais pu l'éviter») et «si seulement j'avais su» pour le regret, donc la logique est parallèle. Mais la traduction littérale transforme «j'aurais dû» en «I would have had to», là où l'anglais dit «should have».

pt.en: Portuguese has the modal perfect in almost the same order as English: devia ter dito (should have said), podia ter evitado (could have avoided). Regret with quem me dera ter sabido (I wish I had known) also transfers well, so the three pieces are familiar.
pt.pt: O português tem o modal perfect quase na mesma ordem do inglês: «devia ter dito» («should have said»), «podia ter evitado» («could have avoided»). O arrependimento com «quem me dera ter sabido» («I wish I had known») também se transfere bem, então os três elementos são familiares.

errores: Using would have inside the if-clause of a third conditional.
Skipping the modal perfect and jumping straight from wish to the third conditional, losing the missed-action step.
Confusing could have and might have when the degree of certainty actually matters to the point.

traducciones.pt: Deixemos os e se por agora.

autochequeo: Does every if-clause use the past perfect, with no would inside it?
Is the modal perfect present as its own step, not skipped?
Are could have and might have used with the right degree of certainty?
Do the three structures appear in a natural sequence, not isolated?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the regret cluster: unreal past, modal perfect, third conditional. Check every if-clause for would have by mistake, and check whether the three structures work together as a sequence. Do not rewrite the text.

es: «*de haberlo sabido*» rendered as *Of having known* instead of *Had I known* or *If I had known*.
de: *hätte kommen sollen* rendered as *would have should come* instead of *should have come*.
it: «*magari*» read as *maybe*: *Maybe I had known!* instead of *If only I had known!*
fr: *à ta place* rendered as *At your place, I would have…* instead of *If I were you* or *In your position*.
pt: *oxalá* rendered as *hopefully*: *Hopefully I had known!* instead of *If only I had known!*
